transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-15
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Alan Morris (CTO, Sable), Priya Kapoor (Head of Platform), Jordan Lee (Security Engineer)
---
[00:00] Maria: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, we got Alan, Priya, Jordan from Sable, and Diego and I from Redwood. How's everyone?
[00:12] Alan: Good, thanks. Excited to dig in — our infra team has a bunch of questions around networking for a Private deployment.
[00:18] Maria: Perfect, Diego will lead the technical bits. High level today is to understand your constraints: regions, CIDR, peering model, kms, and timeline.
[00:28] Diego: Hi all, quick note — I'll try to cover peering options, private endpoints, transit gateway considerations, and typical pitfalls. Feel free to interrupt.
[00:36] Priya: Sounds good. To start, we have strict data residency: primary workloads in us-east-1, backups in eu-west-1. We need the control plane in our account and no internet egress for inference traffic.
[00:48] Jordan: And we require BYOK via our KMS, SOC2 controls, audit logs forwarded to Splunk — standard security checklist.
[00:56] Diego: Great, that aligns with Redwood Private model. Two quick clarifying Qs: do you want Redwood control plane to be in your VPC (private control plane) or host our control plane but with private endpoints?
[01:08] Alan: Preference is private control plane in our AWS account if possible. We want all traffic staying in our VPCs.
[01:14] Maria: Note: Private (customer-managed) control plane is available as an on-prem/VPC deployment. We'll confirm details but that model supports KMS integration and private networking.
[01:24] Diego: Ok, so the options we typically discuss: 1) VPC Peering between your VPC and Redwood-managed VPCs; 2) AWS PrivateLink / Interface Endpoints where Redwood exposes service endpoints into your VPC; 3) Transit Gateway peering/hub for multi-VPC setups; 4) Dedicated deployment where Redwood runs within your account on reserved capacity. Each has tradeoffs.
[01:40] Priya: We're leaning away from peering because of CIDR constraints — our CIDR space is small and already used across many subnets. What are the limits for peering overlap?
[01:50] Diego: Right — AWS disallows overlapping CIDRs for VPC peering. If there's any overlap it's a blocker. For that reason PrivateLink or Transit Gateway are common when you can't restructure CIDRs. PrivateLink uses ENIs in your VPC so no CIDR overlap issue, but it does have limits on number of endpoints and cross-region setup is more manual.
[02:10] Jordan: Can you do PrivateLink cross-account and cross-region? We need endpoints in us-east-1 and eu-west-1.
[02:18] Diego: PrivateLink is regional. For cross-region, we'd deploy endpoints in each region. Cross-account is supported; Redwood would create service in our account and you create VPC endpoints in yours, or with Private deployment we can run the service inside your account and skip cross-account access.
[02:30] Alan: If we host the control plane in our account, do we still need PrivateLink?
[02:34] Diego: If the entire deployment is inside your account — meaning Redwood software runs in your VPCs — you don't need PrivateLink for API traffic. You'd only need it if you're connecting to a Redwood-managed control plane.
[02:44] Priya: What about egress IPs? Our firewall rules expect fixed egress IPs for outbound calls. Does Redwood offer static egress or NAT IPs?
[02:53] Maria: For hosted, egress IPs vary and are not guaranteed. For Private in-customer-account deployments, you control NAT and egress so you can present static IPs via a NAT Gateway or egress proxy. For dedicated hosted with NAT we can discuss static IP pools but it's less common.
[03:09] Jordan: KMS — we need BYOK with keys in our AWS account, and customer-managed key rotation. Any constraints?
[03:16] Diego: Redwood Private supports customer KMS. If the control plane runs in your account, your KMS keys can be used for model encryption and audit trails. For hosted control plane with private endpoints, there are options but cross-account KMS permissions get tricky — we typically recommend customer-managed deployment for strict BYOK.
[03:31] Priya: TLS certs and SSO — we use SAML SSO and need RBAC tied to Okta groups.
[03:38] Maria: We support SAML SSO and RBAC mapping. On Private deployments we can integrate with your IdP directly.
[03:44] Alan: Transit gateway — we already use a TGW for hub-and-spoke. Would Redwood connect via TGW?
[03:50] Diego: Yes, connecting via Transit Gateway is common when you have multiple VPCs. Redwood can peer a VPC attachment to your TGW. That avoids CIDR overlap issues and scales better than many peering connections. Be aware of TGW route table capacity and propagation details.
[04:05] Priya: Any limits on the number of prefixes or routes? Our TGW has custom route limits but we can manage.
[04:11] Diego: Limits are AWS-specific; TGW has route limits per attachment and per route table. For high-scale setups we sometimes suggest using NLB with PrivateLink for predictable scaling. We'll share a recommended architecture.
[04:22] Jordan: Audit logs — can we push request/audit logs to our S3 or to Splunk via Kinesis?
[04:28] Diego: Yes, Private deployments support pushing logs to your S3 and forwarding events. For hosted endpoints we'd provide streaming logs but you'd need to accept data egress. We'll send the log-forwarding guide.
[04:38] Alan: We're also curious about region constraints — some customers want to keep model weights in region and not replicate across. Does Redwood support region pinning?
[04:47] Maria: Yes, you can pin model variants to regions. For Private deployments inside your account, model artifacts stay in your region's S3. For hosted, we have regional clusters but we'll need to confirm residency and replication settings.
[04:58] Priya: Performance — latency SLOs for inference within us-east-1. Any benchmarking we can run?
[05:04] Diego: We can run an in-account POC with a small cluster and run a benchmark harness. Typical plan: spin up a replica, run example workload for 24–72 hours, measure p95/avg latency and tokens/sec. We'll need sample traffic and prompts.
[05:19] Alan: Timeline — we want a POC in 6–8 weeks, production in Q3. Is that feasible?
[05:24] Maria: Yes, that's within typical timelines: 2–4 weeks for network and infra setup (depending on approvals), 2–4 weeks for POC benchmarking and tuning. We'll outline milestones.
[05:32] Priya: About pricing — rough delta between Dedicated and Private?
[05:36] Maria: Dedicated (Redwood-managed dedicated capacity) is committed cost with reserved GPU pools; Private (customer-managed) has platform fee plus infra you run in your account. We'll share an estimate sheet.
[05:46] Jordan: Security review — our legal/security team will want SOC2, ISO certs, penetration test reports, and a data flow diagram.
[05:54] Maria: We'll attach SOC2 report and a standard data flow diagram. For penetration tests we can share our last red team summary and coordinate NDA if you need more detail.
[06:03] Diego: One technical caveat: if you go with PrivateLink we need to ensure ENI quotas in your subnets. ENI scarcity can cause endpoint creation failures. For large setups we recommend /26 or larger subnets for endpoint ENIs.
[06:17] Priya: Good to know — our subnets are mostly /24 and a few /26s. We'll verify.
[06:22] Alan: CIDR overlap potential — we might have to reassign a few ranges which is painful. If Transit Gateway works with us, that reduces re-CIDRing.
[06:31] Diego: Correct. TGW with route propagation avoids direct VPC peering restrictions. If you already have a TGW, attaching Redwood VPCs (or running Redwood inside your account and attaching) is simplest.
[06:40] Maria: Quick note on firewall: do you need outbound calls to external services? e.g., metrics to third-party SaaS?
[06:46] Jordan: No external egress except to our Splunk ingestion endpoint and to AWS S3 in eu-west-1 for backup.
[06:53] Diego: Those can be whitelisted via NAT or VPC endpoints to S3. We'll include sample route/NAT config.
[07:01] Priya: Any changes for model updates and rollouts? We want controlled rollouts and canary traffic.
[07:07] Maria: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts and A/B routing. In Private we can configure the same rollout policies. Canary traffic routing is an app-level config and works the same across deployment models.
[07:16] Alan: Great. A few small questions that came from our infra team offline: 1) Will Redwood need any IAM roles in our account? 2) Do you support cross-account assume-role for automation?
[07:26] Diego: For a customer-managed deployment, you'll create IAM roles and policies we provide and Redwood automation will assume roles with least privileges. For fully-hosted we use cross-account roles for certain integrations; we can provide the exact policy templates.
[07:38] Priya: About secrets and keys: we use AWS Secrets Manager. Can Redwood integrate with it for DB creds?
[07:44] Diego: Yes, integrations exist — Redwood can read secrets from Secrets Manager with IAM permission. For extra security we recommend restricting the KMS key access to only service principals used by the cluster.
[07:55] Jordan: Any compliance differences if we host in eu-west-1 vs us-east-1 for backup storage? We have GDPR concerns.
[08:02] Maria: We'll keep backups in the region you specify. For GDPR, we'd store EU data in eu-west-1. For cross-region backups we can encrypt with separate KMS keys and provide data processing agreements.
[08:14] Alan: Ok, next steps — send network diagram, SOC2, sample IAM policies, and pricing. Diego, can you prepare the draft peering/endpoint diagram?
[08:22] Diego: Yep, I will. I'll include three options: TGW attachment, PrivateLink endpoints, and in-account deployment with NAT config.
[08:30] Priya: We'll also send our CIDR map and current TGW IDs, plus contact for our networking lead.
[08:36] Maria: Perfect. Any other blockers?
[08:40] Jordan: Not right now — just need to validate CIDR and ENI quotas. Also want to run our security checklist against your SOC2 docs.
[08:48] Maria: We'll follow up with the docs and set a deep-dive for Apr 22 with your infra team.
[08:53] Alan: Thanks, appreciate it.
[08:55] Maria: Quick recap: action items and owners — Maria will send security and pricing, Diego will produce the peering diagram and route samples, Jordan will share CIDR ranges and TGW info. We'll schedule follow-up.
[09:08] Priya: One more thing — do you have a reference for NAT/static egress approaches? We want an architecture note.
[09:14] Diego: We'll include a NAT egress pattern and a proxy egress pattern (egress through an ALB/NAT with Elastic IPs), plus how to wire Splunk ingestion securely.
[09:24] Alan: If we proceed with POC, who will run it on Redwood side? AE+SE?
[09:29] Maria: AE+SE for onboarding, solutions engineer and SRE for the POC. We'll include an outline of deliverables.
[09:35] Diego: Anything else from Sable?
[09:38] Jordan: Not now. We'll review the docs and get back.
[09:41] Maria: Thanks everyone — we'll send notes in the next 24 hours.
[09:45] Alan: Thanks, bye.
[09:46] Maria: Bye.
---
Notes: Transcript includes some transcription artifacts and short interruptions. Key technical items: prefer customer-managed control plane in account, TGW preferred to avoid CIDR overlap, PrivateLink for regional endpoints where needed, BYOK via customer KMS, static egress handled by customer NAT/GW, SOC2 and data residency docs to be provided.
